title: Yggra
description: A literature taxonomy of agent improvement mechanisms and multimodal capability pathways.
coverage: Fifteen representative papers and six editorial capability pathways; not a comprehensive review.
annotation_kind: Editorial summaries of cited papers; not independent replications.
relationship_semantics: Branch parent_id expresses taxonomy; paper branch_ids express classification. Pathway stages are editorial capability targets, not chronology, prerequisites, paper ancestry, or agent-version lineage. Capability gains alone do not establish persistent self-improvement.

question_filter.meaning: Highlight mechanism-relevant work. Exclusion does not mean evidence of absence.

status_definitions.tested: Tested within the specific experimental scope in the note; not a general proof.
status_definitions.mechanism: The mechanism is present or provides indirect support; the research question is not fully isolated.
status_definitions.unknown: The atlas has not verified evidence for this question; not evidence of absence.
status_definitions.outside: Outside the core method's stated scope.

questions.title: Can capabilities be inherited?
questions.description: Track what experience is retained and whether it remains useful in descendants, other tasks, or different models.
questions.criterion: Transfer evaluations, component transplants, removal studies, and rollback experiments.

questions.title: Can lineage improve search?
questions.description: Distinguish recording history from using ancestors, branches, and failed attempts to choose the next modification.
questions.criterion: Equal-budget comparisons with linear improvement and ordinary archive search.

questions.title: Do descendants become better improvers?
questions.description: Distinguish higher task scores, an editable improver, and measured gains in the ability to produce useful changes.
questions.criterion: Compare ancestors and descendants under the same future search budget.

all.title: Agent evolution research
all.summary: Two organizing lenses: how agents improve and which capabilities they acquire. Taxonomy links are classifications; capability pathways are research targets.

harness.title: Harness improvement
harness.summary: Improve the system around a model: prompts, tools, memory, skills, and agent code. Mechanisms may overlap.

evolution.title: Archive search & branch evolution
evolution.summary: Use prior candidates or selected parents to generate, evaluate, and retain new agents. Actual version inheritance is a harness improvement mechanism within this branch.

iterative.title: Iterative optimization
iterative.summary: Turn evaluation feedback into updates to prompts, code, and other variables in the current system.

memory.title: Experience accumulation
memory.summary: Retain experience as retrievable reflections or code skills for reuse in later attempts and tasks.

joint.title: Model–harness co-optimization
joint.summary: Compilation and optimization may target both a language-model pipeline and learnable model parameters. Fine-tuning is optional; evidence depends on the configuration.

foundation.title: Related foundations
foundation.summary: Foundational methods that help define the scope of self-improvement. Revising an output within a task does not establish persistent agent capability growth.

capabilities.title: Capability pathways
capabilities.summary: Editorial routes through capabilities that generalist agents may acquire. Stages describe research targets, not historical ancestry or demonstrated self-improvement.

grounded-perception.title: Grounded perception
grounded-perception.summary: Connect observations and instructions to objects, locations, and possible interactions.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Measure referent localization and downstream action success on unseen objects and viewpoints; compare with a 2D-only baseline.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Store reusable object and affordance knowledge, then test whether that memory transfers to new scenes.
pathway.reading_status: Direct readings are listed for lectures 2–3.

multimodal-reasoning.title: Multimodal reasoning
multimodal-reasoning.summary: Combine language and sensory evidence when neither alone determines the answer.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Test held-out compositions and conflicting inputs. Remove or shuffle each modality to establish whether performance depends on grounding.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Optimize fusion prompts and evidence-routing code; compare variants under the same model and inference budget.
pathway.reading_status: CLIP and Winoground are listed for lecture 5. Readings for lectures 12–15 are TBD.

generative-communication.title: Generative communication
generative-communication.summary: Produce and iteratively edit visual or spoken outputs under user control.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Under a fixed interaction budget, measure constraint satisfaction and requested-edit success, including preservation of unchanged content.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Retain useful feedback as edit strategies and test reuse across tasks; distinguish one output revision from a persistent agent update.
pathway.reading_status: Direct readings for lectures 6–9 are TBD; no generation paper has been added from this syllabus.

world-models.title: Temporal & causal world models
world-models.summary: Reason about how a world changes and which actions could produce a desired outcome.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Compare equal-budget planning with and without a predictive model on changed dynamics. Test causal claims on held-out interventions separately from prediction accuracy.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Use failed rollouts to propose planner changes, retain alternative variants, and test whether archive-guided selection improves later planning.
pathway.reading_status: Scene graphs and SayPlan are earlier-course bridges from lecture 3, not demonstrations of learned causal world models. Direct readings for lectures 10–11 and 24–25 are TBD.

embodied-action.title: Embodied action
embodied-action.summary: Turn multimodal understanding into physical actions that adapt to contact and disturbance.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Measure success on unseen objects and perturbations; ablate visual, language, and tactile feedback separately.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Transfer a learned skill library to new objects or embodiments; test retained task success and adaptation cost.
pathway.reading_status: Where2Act and optional SayPlan are listed for lecture 3. They bridge to later action topics; direct readings for lectures 18–20 and 24 are TBD.

structured-reasoning.title: Structured & scientific reasoning
structured-reasoning.summary: Work with tables, charts, symbolic relations, and scientific measurements while preserving their structure.

pathway.stage_order_semantics: Editorial capability targets. Order is not a historical lineage, a required prerequisite sequence, or a claim of universal progress.
pathway.suggested_evaluation: Hold out relation compositions or acquisition settings. Measure answer accuracy, structural consistency, and intervention predictions separately.
pathway.improvement_hypothesis: Evolve parsers, verifiers, and analysis workflows; test whether improved components transfer to a new domain without changing the evaluation budget.
pathway.reading_status: Winoground is an earlier-course bridge for compositional evaluation, not a scientific-domain method. Direct readings for lectures 21–23 and 25 are TBD.

papers.name: DGM
papers.title: Darwin Gödel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
papers.mechanism: Select a parent agent from a historical archive, modify its code, and evaluate the resulting variant on coding tasks.

q1.note: Descendants inherit code, and designs were tested across models. The causal contribution of individual inherited capabilities still requires separate tests.

q2.note: Archive exploration was compared with linear updates and greedy parent selection. Evidence covers the archive and parent-selection strategies.

q3.note: Improved agents continue self-modification, with a fixed initial-improver baseline. General gains in improvement efficiency require further validation.

papers.name: Hyperagents
papers.title: Hyperagents
papers.mechanism: Place the task agent and its modifying meta agent in one editable program, allowing the mechanism that generates future improvements to evolve.

q1.note: Meta-level improvements were tested for cross-domain transfer and cross-run reuse. Not every inherited component received a causal ablation.

q2.note: Open-ended archive exploration baselines were compared. The independent benefit of lineage-depth selection remains to be verified.

q3.note: Section 5.2 freezes a transferred meta agent and measures its ability to generate better agents using imp@50.

papers.limitation: Some final cross-run differences were not statistically significant. The results do not establish universal or unbounded self-acceleration.

papers.name: ADAS
papers.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
papers.mechanism: A meta agent programs new agents using an expanding archive of candidates and feeds evaluation results into the next design round.

q1.note: Whole designs were tested across domains and models. This does not isolate the causal effect of component inheritance.

q2.note: The candidate archive informs search. This differs from isolating the value of explicit parent–child lineage.

q3.note: The meta-level process in Meta Agent Search remains fixed.

papers.name: Reflexion
papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.mechanism: Convert task feedback into verbal reflections stored in episodic memory for later attempts, without updating model weights.

q1.note: Reflective memory was tested for its benefit on later attempts. This does not establish inheritance between independent descendants.

q2.note: The core method does not search a parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: A fixed framework executes reflection and update steps.

papers.name: Voyager
papers.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
papers.mechanism: Improve programs using Minecraft environment feedback and store successful behaviors in a retrievable, composable code-skill library.

q1.note: Learned skills were transferred to a new world to solve new tasks. The evidence concerns skill reuse.

q2.note: Skill retrieval and composition do not depend on parent–child version-lineage search.

q3.note: The skill-generation and improvement framework remains fixed.

papers.name: TextGrad
papers.title: TextGrad: Automatic “Differentiation” via Text
papers.mechanism: Backpropagate language-model-generated textual feedback through a computation graph to optimize prompts, code, and other system variables.

q1.note: Variable optimization gains were demonstrated. Evidence of descendant capability inheritance has not been verified in this atlas.

q2.note: The computation graph describes feedback propagation, not agent-version ancestry.

q3.note: The original TextGrad uses a predefined optimization framework.

papers.name: DSPy
papers.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
papers.mechanism: Express language-model pipelines as declarative modules, then compile them by optimizing demonstrations and other learnable parameters against a target metric.

q1.note: Compiled pipeline performance was tested. Module reuse and strict capability inheritance require further distinction.

q2.note: Parent–child agent-lineage search is not the original paper's central contribution.

q3.note: The compilation process does not target autonomous rewriting of its optimizer.

papers.name: Self-Refine
papers.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
papers.mechanism: Alternate feedback and revision with the same language model to improve the current task output.

q1.note: The study concerns within-task output refinement, not persistent descendant capabilities.

q2.note: The core process is linear refinement, not agent-version lineage search.

q3.note: The feedback and revision procedure remains fixed.

papers.name: ViT
papers.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
papers.mechanism: Applies a Transformer directly to sequences of image patches, then transfers a pretrained visual representation to image recognition tasks.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: Visual backbone training and transfer do not establish agent version inheritance or autonomous improvement of the training process.

papers.name: CLIP
papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.mechanism: Learns image and text representations by matching image-caption pairs, enabling natural-language descriptions to specify visual concepts for zero-shot transfer.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: Pretraining and zero-shot transfer supply a perception capability; they do not demonstrate agents inheriting learned improvements from parent versions.

papers.name: VGGT
papers.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
papers.mechanism: A feed-forward network jointly infers camera parameters, depth maps, point maps, and 3D point tracks from one or many scene views.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: Provides geometric perception and transferable visual features; it is not a mechanism for evolving an agent or its improver.

papers.name: 3D Dynamic Scene Graphs
papers.title: 3D Dynamic Scene Graphs: Actionable Spatial Perception with Places, Objects, and Humans
papers.mechanism: Builds hierarchical scene graphs from visual-inertial observations, representing places, objects, moving agents, and their spatial and temporal relations.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: An evolving map records changes in the environment; this alone does not show persistent improvement of an agent's capabilities or inheritance between agent versions.

papers.name: Where2Act
papers.title: Where2Act: From Pixels to Actions for Articulated 3D Objects
papers.mechanism: Learns from simulated interactions to predict localized pushing and pulling affordances from image and depth observations of articulated objects.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: Interaction data trains a reusable affordance predictor, but the work does not establish inheritance across agent generations or an improver that improves itself.

papers.name: SayPlan
papers.title: SayPlan: Grounding Large Language Models using 3D Scene Graphs for Scalable Robot Task Planning
papers.mechanism: Combines LLM search over hierarchical 3D scene graphs, classical path planning, and simulator feedback to revise infeasible robot task plans.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: Iterative replanning repairs a task plan; it does not by itself demonstrate that a persistent planner or its descendants become better improvers.

papers.name: Winoground
papers.title: Winoground: Probing Vision and Language Models for Visio-Linguistic Compositionality
papers.mechanism: Evaluates compositional understanding by matching two images to captions with the same words arranged in different orders.

q1.note: This entry supplies a capability foundation or evaluation. Agent-descendant capability inheritance is outside its core scope.

q2.note: The method does not test search over parent–child agent-version lineage.

q3.note: The work does not test whether descendants become better at generating future agent improvements.

papers.limitation: A diagnostic benchmark can test a proposed capability gain; the benchmark itself is not a learning, inheritance, or recursive improvement method.

cross_cutting_facets.title: Data, training & evaluation
cross_cutting_facets.application: Hold data access, training resources, and evaluation budgets constant when comparing agent variants.

cross_cutting_facets.application: Assess permission adherence, privacy, controllability, and user correction across all capability routes.
